description: Selenium is a chemical element with symbol Se and atomic number 34. It has various physical appearances, including a brick-red powder, a vitreous black solid, and a grey metallic-looking form. It was discovered in 1817 by Jöns Jacob Berzelius, who noted its similarity to tellurium.
uses: The chief commercial uses for selenium are glassmaking and pigments. Selenium is a semiconductor used in photocells, and it is still used in some types of DC power surge protectors and fluorescent quantum dots. Selenium is also listed as an ingredient in multivitamins and dietary supplements, and is a component of antioxidant enzymes and deiodinase enzymes.
characteristics: Selenium forms several allotropes that interconvert with temperature changes. It can appear as an amorphous brick-red powder, a black vitreous form with polymeric rings, or gray selenium with a hexagonal crystal lattice. Gray selenium is a semiconductor showing appreciable photoconductivity and is insoluble in carbon disulfide, while other forms are insulators and soluble in carbon disulfide.
